title: Natural variation in DXR expression is associated with apical hook bending under NaCl stress in Arabidopsis thaliana
content:
Abstract
Successful soil emergence requires the establishment of an apical hook during skotomorphogenesis. Soil salinity disrupts this process, but the mechanisms linking environmental stress to hook growth remain unclear. Here, we employed a genome-wide association study across Arabidopsis accessions to identify a locus associated with variation in the salt-induced reduction of apical hook curvature. Fine-mapping revealed genetic variation in the promoter of 1-DEOXY-D-XYLULOSE 5-PHOSPHATE REDUCTOISOMERASE (DXR), which encodes the first committed enzyme of the plastid-localized methylerythritol phosphate (MEP) pathway. Accessions carrying an alternative promoter haplotype exhibited elevated DXR expression and stronger hook-bending under salt stress. Salt treatment and loss of function of the transcriptional repressor PHYTOCHROME INTERACTING FACTOR1 (PIF1) additively increased DXR transcript levels, and seedlings of the pif1-2 mutant exhibited greater apical hook angles under salt stress. This phenotype was suppressed by inhibition of DXR activity, indicating that an increased MEP pathway flux reduces salt sensitivity in pif1-2 seedlings. Across accessions, DXR expression positively correlated with hook curvature under salt stress, further strengthening the link between DXR and modulation of hook bending under salt stress. Together, these findings identify plastid metabolism as a regulatory layer linking environmental stress to altered skotomorphogenesis, and raise important questions about how etioplast-derived signals interact with growth-control networks in the dark.
